newsitem.title: FRANCE: France raises 96 grain crop estimate to 61 mln T.
newsitem.headline: France raises 96 grain crop estimate to 61 mln T.

text.p: The French farm ministry said on Friday it had raised its estimate for the 1996 grain crop to 61 million tonnes from a previous target of 57.3 million, confirming earlier grain industry reports.
This would compare with a 1995 grain harvest of 53.6 milion tonnes.
In its September report, the ministry also raised to 34.1 million tonnes its forecast for the soft wheat crop from a previous estimate of 31.3 million and 29.8 million in 1995.
The new estimate assumes the soft wheat yield would rise to 7.16 tonnes per hectare from 6.56 tonnes forecast last month and 6.61 tonnes in 1995.
Wheat area is seen declining to 4.766 million hectares from 4.772 million forecast last month but should rise from 4.513 million in 1995.
Barley output was put at 9.3 million tonnes against some 8.7 million tonnes forecast last month and from 7.7 million tonnes produced last year.
The new estimate assumes a barley yeld of 6.09 tonnes against 5.68 tonnes last month and 5.54 tonnes last year.
Total barley area is seen rising to 1.53 million hectares from 1.52 million hectares last month and 1.39 million last year.
The maize crop was revised to 13.8 million tonnes from 13.6 million tonnes last month and 12.8 million tonnes last year.
The estimate assumes a maize yield of 7.99 tonnes per hectare against 7.88 tonnes last month and 7.72 tonnes last year.
Maize area is forecast at 1.73 million hectares, unchanged from last month but up from 1.66 million last year.
On Wednesday, France's grain office ONIC forecast a 1996 grain crop of 60 million tonnes, a level that would match production levels before the reform of the Common Agricultural Policy.
